name: Chip supply
value: US and China extend control pauses to 10 Jan
summary: US and China both extend pauses on chip-related export controls to 10 Jan; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage found
state: China's commerce ministry said on 9 Nov it would keep its expanded rare-earth export controls suspended until 10 Jan while talks with Washington continue (The Star; S&P Global). On the same day the US Bureau of Industry and Security extended its pause on the Affiliates Rule, which widens chip-export licensing to subsidiaries of listed firms, to 10 Jan 2027 (Dechert). Rare-earth licensing from April 2025 remains in force, and no TSMC or Samsung stoppage was found as of 12 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Electronics, car and defence manufacturers that rely on Chinese rare earths or ship chip tools to China face the most uncertainty, with both pauses now set to lapse on 10 Jan unless extended again.
rubric_hit: Export controls on rare earths and chip tools still in force or paused only to 10 Jan meet Watch; no major TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: The Star — China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January
S&P Global — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027
Dechert — A reprieve, not a repeal: BIS extends the Affiliates Rule pause

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
